feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. The candidate is iteration 3 with one change: kd 0.3 to 0.4, with kp 2.5, ki 0.2, base_speed 1.0, sensor_size 0.012 and the geometry unchanged. Iterations 0 to 3 all ended off track (240 trials), with progress 0.10 to 0.16 and max_error 0.061 to 0.067 m. Iteration 3 (score 52.06) had steering_oscillation 0.139 on the s-bend and 0.143 on the slalom, against 0.075 on the oval. Its progress stayed near 0.15 on the s-bend despite kp dropping from 4.0 to 2.5, so gain is not the main limit. Iteration 1 suggested kd 0.3 reduced oval oscillation, but that run also changed base_speed and ki, so the damping effect is plausible rather than proven. This candidate is a clean single-lever test of damping on the bends. It is valid, and it is the best test available for the oscillation hypothesis. Read the race as follows. If steering_oscillation on the s-bend and slalom falls clearly below 0.12 and progress rises above 0.2, keep kd 0.4 and raise base_speed in steps (1.2, then 1.4), since a finish needs about 1.5 m/s. If oscillation drops but progress stays near 0.15, the limit is geometric: the sensors sit only 0.05 m ahead of the axle, so the robot reacts late on curves. Then move the sensor row forward (y to about 0.07) before changing gains again. If oscillation is unchanged, the damping hypothesis is weak and kd should not be pushed further.
requested_changes: After race 4: if steering_oscillation on the s-bend and slalom falls below about 0.12 and progress rises above 0.2, keep controller.kd at 0.4 and raise controller.base_speed in steps (1.0 to 1.2 to 1.4). Iteration 3 showed the bend oscillation at 0.139 and 0.143.

After race 4: if progress stays near 0.15 on the s-bend while oscillation falls, change geometry.sensor_positions y from 0.05 to about 0.07 for all five sensors, keeping the x values and weights. The sensors sit only 0.05 m ahead of the axle, and every gain change so far has left progress near 0.15.

After race 4: if steering_oscillation does not fall below 0.139 on the s-bend, do not raise kd further. Return kd to 0.3 and treat the drift as geometric or as a fixed motor-mismatch problem, which may need ki above 0.2 (iteration 3 used 0.2).
